items.title: U.N. report finds migratory freshwater fish declined 81% since 1970

featured_image.name: Migratory freshwater fish decline 76 percent since 1970, new ...

items.description: Migratory freshwater fish populations have declined by 81 percent worldwide since 1970, according to a new United Nations assessment that calls the crisis one of the steepest drops recorded for any major vertebrate group. The report, released this week at the CMS COP15 wildlife conference in Campo Grande, Brazil, identifies 325 species in urgent need of coordinated international conservation action.[1][2][3]

items.title: Iran signals preference for Vance as US negotiator, rejecting Witkoff and Kushner

featured_image.name: Vance’s active VP role is a historical rarity, 'huge asset' to US, says top  GOP ally

items.description:
Iran has signaled to the Trump administration that it prefers to negotiate with Vice President JD Vance rather than other senior officials, rejecting renewed engagement with special envoy Steve Witkoff and presidential son-in-law Jared Kushner, according to a CNN report citing two regional sources.[1][2]

The message was conveyed through back channels to mediating countries, with Iranian representatives expressing that talks involving Witkoff and Kushner would not be productive given what sources described as a "deficit of trust". The collapse of earlier nuclear negotiations in Geneva, followed within days by US and Israeli military strikes that began on February 28, left Tehran deeply skeptical of the pair's intentions.[3][4][5][1]

items.title: Trump sets May 14-15 for rescheduled Beijing summit with Xi

featured_image.name: Trump signals possible delay to Beijing summit as U.S. pressures China to  help reopen Strait of Hormuz

items.description:
President Donald Trump will travel to Beijing on May 14 and 15 for a rescheduled summit with Chinese President Xi Jinping, the White House announced Wednesday, setting firm dates for a trip that had been thrown into uncertainty by the ongoing U.S. and Israeli war against Iran.[1]

The visit was originally planned for March 31 to April 2 but was postponed as Trump said he needed to remain in Washington to oversee military operations, known as Operation Epic Fury. The announcement comes even as the conflict in Iran continues and the administration presses Tehran to accept a ceasefire proposal.[2][3][1]

items.title: Global stocks surge as US sends 15-point ceasefire plan to Iran

featured_image.name: Wall Street indexes rally after Trump postpones strikes on Iran's ...

items.description:
Stock markets around the world rallied on Wednesday as investors reacted to reports that the United States had delivered a 15-point ceasefire proposal to Iran, raising hopes for a diplomatic resolution to the nearly month-old conflict that has roiled global markets and sent energy prices soaring.

The S&P 500 rose 1.1% in early trading, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average climbed more than 500 points and the Nasdaq Composite gained 1.3%, according to the Associated Press. In Europe, Germany's DAX advanced 1.7%, France's CAC 40 climbed 1.4%, and Britain's FTSE 100 rose 0.9%. Asian markets posted even sharper gains, with Japan's Nikkei 225 surging nearly 3% and South Korea's Kospi jumping more than 3%. Oil prices fell sharply, with Brent crude dropping more than 5%.[1][2][3][4]

items.title: Gold surges as oil slump eases inflation fears

featured_image.name: Gold jumps 2% as oil slump eases inflation fears amid Trump Iran talks

items.description:
Gold prices climbed sharply on Wednesday as a steep decline in oil prices eased inflation concerns and tempered expectations for interest rate hikes by the Federal Reserve, even as mixed signals over a potential U.S.-Iran ceasefire kept markets on edge.

Spot gold rose nearly 2% to around $4,551 per ounce, while gold futures for April delivery jumped more than 3%, according to CNBC. The rally came as oil prices sank more than 5% on optimism that Washington was pursuing a diplomatic path to pause the conflict, with Brent crude falling to roughly $99 per barrel and West Texas Intermediate dropping to around $88.[1][2]

items.title: AI detects landslide risks years in advance using satellite radar data

featured_image.name: AI Predicts Landslides with Enhanced Precision

items.description:
Around the village of Kimtang in central Nepal, cracks run through concrete steps and trees grow at odd angles — signs that the ground is shifting beneath residents' feet. Scientists at the University of Melbourne have used artificial intelligence to analyze satellite radar data and confirm what villagers long suspected: their homes sit atop an unstable slope at high risk of a devastating landslide. The AI marked the danger zone in bright red on a color map, a warning that could prove lifesaving.[1][2]

The Nepal project is part of a growing wave of research applying AI to one of the world's most destructive and difficult-to-predict natural hazards. In the first two months of 2026 alone, 91 fatal landslides killed more than 800 people worldwide, according to data tracked by Eos. Researchers across multiple continents are now racing to deploy machine learning systems that can detect the subtle ground movements that precede catastrophic slope failures.[3]

items.title: Iran mocks US ceasefire plan, says Americans 'negotiating with yourselves'

featured_image.name: Americans were negotiating with themselves': Iran mocks US ...

items.description:
President Trump's assertion that the United States is engaged in productive negotiations with Iran to end the month-old war has been met with open derision from Tehran, where an Iranian military spokesperson on Wednesday said the Americans "are negotiating with yourselves."[1]

Lt. Col. Ebrahim Zolfaghari, speaking in a prerecorded video on Iranian state television, dismissed Trump's diplomatic overtures. "Don't dress up your defeat as an agreement. Your era of empty promises has come to an end," he said, according to the Associated Press. His remarks came shortly after the Trump administration delivered a 15-point ceasefire plan to Iran through Pakistani intermediaries.[2][3][1]
